notes:
clock: one place decides the time, and it says when the timezone did not apply

A box with system.timezone set to America/Sao_Paulo was still computing every
schedule in UTC. Measured through the browser at 18:41 local: BirdTunes
reported "Horário de silêncio" with quiet hours starting at 20:00, which only
holds if the box believes it is 21:41.

zoneinfo reads the system tz database. The image installs with
--no-install-recommends and never asks for tzdata, so
ZoneInfo("America/Sao_Paulo") raises; birdtunes._now caught it, logged a
warning nobody reads and returned the system clock. Choosing a timezone in
Settings therefore did nothing, and no screen said so. Three hours of offset
account for quiet hours effectively starting at 17:00 and a 12:30 routine
playing at 09:30.

core.clock gains zona(), now() and state(). zona() separates a missing tz
database from an unknown zone name by testing a zone every database carries, so
the screen can say which of the two happened. state() returns the box's local
time, the zone actually in force, the offset, the drift against the viewer's
clock and a ready-made sentence. birdtunes._now delegates to it, removing the
second copy of the decision that hid the failure.

tzdata becomes a required dependency rather than something the distribution
might have shipped: a box whose purpose is doing things at the right time
cannot depend on that.

The dashboard gains a clock card, first in the grid. It ticks from the epoch
the server reported plus elapsed time, never from the browser's own clock -- a
clock mirroring the viewer would always look right and would have hidden this.
It warns when the configured zone is not in force and when the two clocks
disagree by more than five minutes.

Also: the device card built "N found on your network" inline instead of asking
for a key, so it showed English on a Portuguese dashboard. A guard now compares
every t() key the views request against the translations, ignoring runtime-built
prefixes.

system.notes:
Telas: nove avisos usavam uma classe de aviso que o tema não define

O tema define .notice--warn e .notice--error. O código escrevia
.notice--warning, que não existe em lugar nenhum. CSS não reclama de classe
desconhecida -- ela simplesmente não pinta, e o aviso sai com a borda cinza de
uma caixa qualquer.

Os nove: gerenciamento de pacotes desligado, atualizações desligadas, falha ao
conferir atualização, senha do SSH não configurada, horário de silêncio, faixas
incompatíveis, sem yt-dlp em duas telas, e o baixador velho.

Um teste guardava o nome errado -- ele documentava o defeito em vez de pegá-lo,
e por isso a suíte dizia que estava tudo certo enquanto nenhum desses avisos
tinha cor. O que faltava era comparar as classes que o código usa com as que o
tema define; test_aviso_pintado_de_aviso.py compara, para qualquer modificador
de aviso, hoje e nos próximos.

Medido depois do conserto: borda em color(srgb 0.775 0.700 0.507) no lugar do
cinza #dde3e6 de antes.

Suíte: 1211 passando, 7 pulando.
